solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ammunition and money, when in US, stolen

parts.note: bucks is American slang for dollars, money in the US
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: A gun-runner's haul: weapons and cash, swiped while in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead shot of the size used for deer hunting is a kind of ammunition fired from shotguns.

clue.text: Break in needing food to lift, given life if found out

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the word for food means writing it upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: grub is informal for food

indicators.note: the word if is driven out of the word life, leaving only its outer pair

explanation.surface: A burglar hungry for a snack, facing a life sentence if caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found out' removes IF from LIFE, leaving LE.
explanation.definitionFit: To burgle a house is to enter it illegally to steal, a break-in.

clue.text: Warning mounted soldiers seen south of hiding place

indicators.note: in a down clue, south of means placed below, so the soldiers come after the hiding place

parts.note: a cave is a classic place to hide

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means the soldiers are written going upwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: A sentry warns that cavalry have been spotted beyond the hideout.
explanation.definitionFit: A caveat is a cautionary proviso, a formal note of caution.

clue.text: Taking back 'It's permitted to put together weapon'

indicators.note: taking back means the letters of the first word are read backwards

parts.note: the letters of it's, ignoring the apostrophe
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: Someone retracting a statement that assembling a weapon is allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking back' turns ITS into STI; 'put together' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a thin-bladed dagger, a stabbing weapon.

clue.text: Just working to get tips: lazy

parts.note: on means functioning or working, as a switched-on machine

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its two end letters

explanation.surface: An idle worker who does the job merely for the gratuities.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and only are synonyms in the sense of merely.

clue.text: Ask for call back within days

indicators.note: within means the reversed word sits between the two day letters

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for day, so two of them stand for days

indicators.note: back means the word for call is written in reverse

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them

explanation.surface: A request to have someone phone again inside a few days.
explanation.definitionFit: To demand something is to ask for it forcefully, an insistent request.

clue.text: Note mistake — or go by

parts.note: E is one of the musical notes
a lapse is a slip or error

explanation.surface: Either jot down an error or let it slide.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to pass or go by; to elapse is the formal verb for that.

clue.text: Your parts engineering team's in purple

indicators.note: the old word for your parts the rearranged letters, sitting between them
engineering means the letters of the team's word are worked into a new order

parts.note: thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: A slightly odd line about your share of an engineering team dressed in purple.
explanation.walkthrough: THY is the archaic form of 'your', a convention worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: The gem is a violet variety of quartz, so its name is used for a purple colour.

clue.text: Dashing stud role arising for collector of dirty films

indicators.note: dashing suggests something thrown about at speed, so the letters of stud are scrambled
in a down clue, arising means the word for role is written upwards

parts.note: a part is an actor's role

explanation.surface: A handsome stud lands a lead role in some smutty films.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dashing' turns STUD into DUST; 'arising' turns PART into TRAP. The 'dirty films' are thin layers of grime, not blue movies.
explanation.definitionFit: A dust trap is a corner or ornament that gathers grime, thin dirty layers of dust.

clue.text: It puts paid to the rest of the men

definitions.text: It puts paid to the rest of the men

parts.words: It puts paid to the rest of the men
parts.note: the rest is the soldiers' sleep, ended by the morning bugle call

explanation.surface: Something that finishes off all the remaining soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the rest of the men' reads as 'the remaining men', but it means the troops' sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: The bugle call that wakes soldiers in the morning ends their night's sleep.

clue.text: Appears clumsily to have dropped a batch of documents

indicators.note: clumsily suggests the letters are handled badly and end up in a new order
the letter a is lost from the scrambled word

explanation.surface: Someone seems to have fumbled and let fall a stack of files.
explanation.walkthrough: APPEARS loses one A and the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Papers is a common word for a set of documents, such as identity papers.

clue.text: Explosive stuff company tried to amend

indicators.note: to amend is to alter, so the letters of tried are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A firm attempting to correct some volatile material.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordite is a smokeless propellant used in firearms and shells, an explosive.

clue.text: Goes for what most herbivores go for

definitions.meaning: departs or exits, as one walks out of a room
plant-eaters chiefly feed on foliage from trees and plants

explanation.surface: A light remark about what plant-eating animals prefer.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is departs; the noun sense is foliage, which plant-eaters eat.

clue.text: What shot played — is he out?

indicators.note: played suggests the letters of what shot are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder wondering about a stroke and whether the batsman is dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: HOW'S THAT is the cricket appeal to the umpire asking whether the batsman is out; cricket is a bat-and-ball game popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Fielders shout this standard appeal at the umpire to claim a dismissal.

clue.text: Worry about nothing, ourselves. Just have a good time

indicators.note: about means the word for worry goes round the other letters

parts.note: care means worry or anxiety
O looks like zero, nothing
us means ourselves

explanation.surface: Advice to stop fretting about ourselves and simply enjoy life.
explanation.definitionFit: To carouse is to drink and make merry, enjoying oneself noisily.

clue.text: Slit ends, darns roughly, thread required

definitions.note: taken as plural threads, to match the plural answer

indicators.note: the ends of a word are its first and last letters
roughly suggests the letters of darns are done carelessly, out of order

explanation.surface: Mending a torn seam by darning crudely, with some thread needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lengths of fibre twisted to make rope or yarn are strands, the same as threads.

clue.text: As a whole, East contrarily is cutting aces

indicators.note: cutting means the reversed word slices between the two ace letters

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace, so two of them give aces

indicators.note: contrarily means the word is is turned the other way round

explanation.surface: A bridge-table remark: East, contrary as ever, trumping the aces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As a whole' qualifies the definition: the continent taken entire is what is loosely called the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the continent loosely called the East, taken as a whole.

clue.text: Ear-piercing as dentist drilled right through!

indicators.note: through means the right letter goes into the rearranged letters
drilled suggests the letters of dentist are bored through and rearranged

explanation.surface: A shrill noise as the dentist bores right into a tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident noise is harsh and loud, grating on the ears.

clue.text: Not doing as the doctor ordered

definitions.text: Not doing as the doctor ordered

parts.words: Not doing as the doctor ordered
parts.note: reads as disobeying the doctor, but means doing nothing on medical advice

explanation.surface: A patient who ignores medical instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not doing' looks like disobedience, but it is idleness the doctor has prescribed.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatment of prolonged bed and inactivity, prescribed by a physician.

clue.text: Bearing in mind there's a rig working

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters go inside the word for mind

parts.note: to mind is to care, as in caring about something

indicators.note: working means the letters of a rig are set in motion into a new order

explanation.surface: Remembering that some oil-rig equipment is operating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' turns ARIG into RIAG, placed 'in' CARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage is the way one carries oneself, one's posture or deportment.

clue.text: Secured — the equaliser?

definitions.meaning: a match-levelling goal leaves the score level, a draw

explanation.surface: A football report: the goal that levelled things up was secured.
explanation.definitionFit: Fastened with a knot, and also level on score, as a drawn game.

clue.text: Chap to criticise about most missorting?

indicators.note: about means the word for criticise goes round the rearranged letters

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly

indicators.note: missorting means the letters of most are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A man criticised over misdirecting most of the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missorting' turns MOST into OSTM, which PAN goes 'about'; the question mark hints the chap sorts mail.
explanation.definitionFit: The chap is a mail carrier, a man who delivers letters.

clue.text: Journalist summons meeting on the subject of climbing

indicators.note: meeting means the two pieces join end to end

parts.note: a writ is a legal summons

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word for about is written upwards

parts.note: re means concerning or about

explanation.surface: A reporter receives a court order over an article on mountaineering.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist is a person who produces articles, a kind of author.

clue.text: Beast makes stand, undermining wife

indicators.note: in a down clue, undermining means the stand sits under the wife letter

parts.note: an easel is a stand for a painting

explanation.surface: An animal that takes a stand and subverts a spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The small carnivorous mammal is a beast; the word also suggests a sly person.

clue.text: Concluded: 'Reconnoitred. Entrance must be effected by key'

indicators.note: an entrance into the word for reconnoitred is made by the key letter, which goes inside

parts.note: to case a place is to scout it before a crime
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A burglar's report: the house was scouted, and entry needs a key.
explanation.definitionFit: To have finished or stopped is to have concluded.

clue.text: Return for one ten, free to take break

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: free means the letters of ten are let loose into a new order

parts.note: a rest is a break

explanation.surface: One prisoner of ten, released and taking a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Interest is the financial yield on money lent or invested, a return.

clue.text: Something easy for a meteorologist's forecast?

definitions.meaning: a task done without effort, a doddle
a weather forecaster might predict a light wind

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a weather report is a simple matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a cinch or easy job; literally a light wind a forecaster may predict.

clue.text: A few therefore to be supported by myself

indicators.note: in a down clue, being supported means sitting on top, so the word for myself goes below

parts.note: so means therefore
me is myself

explanation.surface: A modest claim that some things rest on the speaker alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Some, as a determiner, means an unspecified small number, a handful.

clue.text: Delights coming directly from unbridled lust

parts.note: ex is Latin for from, as in ex works

indicators.note: unbridled means the letters of lust are set loose into a new order

explanation.surface: Pleasures arising straight from uncontrolled desire.
explanation.definitionFit: To exult is to rejoice greatly, so both verbs mean takes great joy.

clue.text: That's sweet, little creatures captivating idiot

indicators.note: captivating means the creatures hold the idiot captive inside them

parts.note: moles are small burrowing animals
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Cute small animals charming a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Molasses is the thick dark syrup from sugar refining, a sweet substance.

clue.text: Opinion right-wing male's held

indicators.note: held means the male word is gripped inside the right-wing word

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative, of the political right
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A view that a conservative man holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a held view or hypothesis, an idea about something.

clue.text: Did show in retrospect always lead astray?

indicators.note: in retrospect means looking back, so the word for always is read backwards

parts.note: ever means always

indicators.note: astray means the letters of lead wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Looking back, did someone always lead people wrong?
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retrospect' turns EVER into REVE; 'astray' turns LEAD into ALED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have revealed something is to have shown or disclosed it.
